summary: @onereach/pnpm-audit-junit ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style minified (control-flow-flattening dispatchers, _0xNNNNNN identifiers) and, at install time, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/... into a tempdir, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line obfuscated bundle (rotating string-array via WV8StW, large mixed literal table) whose behavior is not readable as source. The package's advertised purpose is converting pnpm audit output to JUnit XML, which does not require a second JS runtime — fetching Bun exists to execute a payload that plain Node cannot introspect. Additionally, package.json declares files: ['dist'], but setup.mjs and math_init.js are shipped at the tarball root outside the declared publish surface while still wired into the preinstall lifecycle. The combination of alternate-runtime drop, opaque obfuscated executable payload, mismatched declared files, and a stated purpose that does not require any of this constitutes an install-time remote-code-execution dropper against installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
